findings.text: test_a_followup_only_ref_declares_no_section_half cannot fail on the over-registration its name claims to guard: _normalized_section_ref('y@f-1') returns 'y#' and never equals the mentioned 'y#s2', so registering a followup-only ref as a section half would still leave the finding in place and the test green. It functions only as the positive control that _undeclared_wait can return findings for this fixture.

the new clause 'every malformed-ref refusal names the @followup suffix' is false: reckon/_store_section_ops.py:234 still states sections.<id>.links accepts [project:]slug[#section], and _validated_refs at reckon/_store_section_ops.py:435 requires parsed.stage so it refuses a followup-only ref outright — 'set section_depends_on.<sid>' cannot declare y@f-1 through the MCP store op even though the grammar now admits it.

the paragraph and the manifest's negative_control_note claim two further mutations were run and each reddens 'only its own case', but the run's logs directory holds only negative-control.log and negative-control2.log; no log records either mutation, so the 'alone' claim cannot be checked by a later reader.

still unresolved from the prior review: _resolve_plan_ref resolves a y@f-1 ref through dependency_row_state(data, parsed.stage) with stage None, so the read_plan deps surface reports the whole plan's status and drops the followup the grammar now admits; reckon/mcp.py is outside this repair round's declared write paths.
